title: Pad See Ew
subtitle: Thai stir-fried rice noodles with dark soy and egg
excerpt: Thailand's most popular noodle dish: wide rice noodles stir-fried over extreme heat in dark soy sauce with egg, Chinese broccoli, and chicken until the noodles are charred, smoky, and coated in a deeply savoury glaze.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pad see ew (literally 'stir-fried with soy sauce') is one of the most widely eaten street food noodle dishes in Thailand, distinct from pad thai in its use of wide flat rice noodles (sen yai) and dark soy sauce rather than tamarind-based seasoning. The dish is characterised by the technique of allowing the noodles to sit undisturbed in a very hot wok until they char and caramelise; this produces the characteristic smoky, slightly sweet flavour. The high heat required (wok hei) is difficult to achieve on a domestic hob; the solution is to cook in the smallest feasible batches to preserve pan temperature. Dark soy sauce is thicker and sweeter than light soy sauce and essential to the characteristic colour and flavour; it is not interchangeable with regular soy sauce.

content.text: Cook one serving at a time if possible to maintain pan temperature; a crowded wok steams rather than fries. The noodles must be separated before they go into the wok; clumped noodles break rather than fry. Leave them undisturbed in the wok for 30 to 45 seconds so they char slightly before tossing.

items.preparation: wide flat rice noodles; soaked in cold water 30 minutes if dried, or fresh
stalks halved lengthways; substitute Chinese broccoli (kai-lan) if available

content.text: Mix the dark soy, light soy, oyster sauce, and sugar in a small bowl. Have all ingredients ready beside the wok before starting.

Heat a wok over the highest possible heat until smoking. Add the oil. Add the garlic and chicken and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the chicken is cooked. Push to the side. Crack in the eggs and scramble until just set.

Add the noodles and the sauce mixture. Toss to coat, then let the noodles sit undisturbed for 30 to 45 seconds until they char on the bottom. Add the broccoli and toss for 1 minute until just wilted. Serve immediately with white pepper and chilli vinegar on the side.
